dialog.body: City of Newport Finance Department, this is Janet Whitcomb. How may I help you?
Hi, yes, good morning. I have a question about my property tax bill. I got the, um, the bill, and I honestly don't understand the second page.
Certainly. Which part of the second page is giving you trouble?
The installment part. There are four little boxes with dates, and then a total, and the total is not the same as the first box times four. So I'm confused about what I actually owe, and by when.

The bill is divided into quarterly installments. Each installment is due on its stated date. If any portion of the bill is a prior balance, that may be included in the first installment, which can make the amounts uneven. Does the first box look larger than the others?
Hmm. No, the last box is larger. The last one. By, like, a hundred dollars or so.
Then I would need to look at the account. I can do that, but I need the bill number or the property's parcel identification, which should be printed near the top of the first page.
Okay, hold on, let me find the page. I'm in the car, so, one second. [pause] Okay, there's a plat and a lot. Plat is, uh, forty-one. Lot one eighteen.
Thank you. Please give me a moment while I pull that up.
Sure, sure.
All right, I have it. The fourth installment includes an adjustment from a supplemental assessment. That is why it is higher than the other three.
A supplemental. What is a supplemental? Is that a penalty? Because I did not get a penalty, I paid everything last year, on time.
No, it is not a penalty. It is an additional assessment, usually tied to a change in the property's value, such as completed improvements. It is simply added to the bill.
Improvements. We did the porch. Okay. So the porch is the supplemental. I thought a porch was, you know, a repair, not an improvement.
That determination is made by the assessor's office. If you wish to dispute it, they would be the ones to speak with. I can transfer you after we finish here.

Okay, maybe. Let me ask the other thing first. Can I pay part of an installment? Like, a partial payment. Because this quarter is tight, and I would rather send half now and half later than send nothing.
The city does accept partial payments toward a balance. However, interest accrues on any portion that remains unpaid after the due date. So the unpaid part would be charged interest from that date.
So half is allowed, but the other half gets interest. Not a penalty, but interest.
That is correct. Interest is calculated on the overdue amount.
Okay. That I understand. Mostly. And do they apply it to the oldest box first, or whichever box I want?
Payments are applied to the oldest outstanding amount first. Generally it is not something you can direct.

Hm. Okay. Next thing. I heard there's an exemption. For, like, certain people. I think maybe the age one, or the veteran one, I really don't know which I fit. Is there a form? What is the form number?
There are several exemptions, and each has its own application. I cannot tell you which you qualify for without more information. What is the basis you are considering?
Well, I'm in my forties, so not the senior one. My neighbor said there's a, a disability one? Or a veteran one. I'm not a veteran. My brother is. Does that count?
No, a relative's service would not qualify you. The veteran exemption applies to the veteran or, in certain cases, a surviving spouse. Is there a disability involved for yourself?
No. No, I don't think so. So maybe none of them. But I still want the form number, in case. The number. Is there just one exemption form?

No, there is not a single form. The tax assessor's office handles the exemption applications, and they can give you the correct form number for each category. I do not want to read you a number that belongs to a different exemption.
Oh. So the form number depends on the category, and the category depends on me, and I don't have a category.
In effect, yes. If you tell the assessor's office your circumstances, they can advise whether anything applies. Shall I transfer you there?
Yes, please. But wait, one more. Sorry. If I get an exemption later, does the bill I already paid, the half, does that get refunded?
If an exemption is granted and applied to the period, a credit or refund may result. The assessor's office would also be able to explain the timing.

Okay. May result. Okay. I'm sorry, I'm asking a lot. My son has band practice and I'm supposed to be picking up, um, a reed. His clarinet reed broke, the whole thing, and they have a concert, so I'm driving to the music store while I'm doing this.
No need to apologize. I hope you find the right reed. Before I transfer you, may I confirm a number where you can be reached if the call is disconnected?
Sure. It's four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-nine-five.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-nine-five. Thank you, Mr. Cohen. And your first name for the note, please?
Min-jun. M-I-N, dash, J-U-N. Cohen is the usual way.
Thank you. I have noted that you asked about the fourth installment, the supplemental assessment, and partial payments. I am placing you on hold briefly while I connect you.
Okay. Thank you. And the supplemental is the fourth box, right? Not the first?
The fourth, correct.
Okay, the fourth. Got it. I think. Thanks.
